prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” AI video ad maker — the right one depends on what you need (talking‑head avatar vs. animated promo, budget, languages, platforms, speed, brand control). To help, here’s a short buyer’s guide plus top picks by use case.

Quick questions to narrow it down
- Which platform(s) will you advertise on (Facebook/Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn)?
- Style: live‑looking talking head, voiceover + footage, animated/typographic, or highly stylized generative visuals?
- Do you need human avatars and multilingual audio?
- Budget and team size (solo, SMB, enterprise)?
- Do you have assets (footage, images) or want script → video from scratch?

Top options and when to pick each
- Synthesia — Best for professional talking‑head ads with AI presenters. Strengths: realistic avatars, multi‑language voice options, fast script→video. Good for product explainers and localized ads.
- HeyGen (Movio-style) — Similar to Synthesia; often more cost‑flexible and good for quick avatar videos and social ads.
- Pictory — Great for turning scripts or long content into short social clips. Strong automatic captioning and repurposing tools for social formats.
- InVideo — Robust template library, easy editing + AI-assisted copy/scene suggestions. Good all‑rounder for marketers who want quick, polished ads.
- Canva (Video / Magic Studio) — Easiest and most accessible; excellent for social ad templates, brand kit support, cheap/free tier for small budgets.
- Lumen5 — Very focused on text→video for social posts and ads; simple workflow and many templates for short promos.
- VEED.IO — Editor with AI subtitles, auto‑translations, quick repurposing; good if you want editing + AI helpers in one tool.
- Runway / Kaiber — Best for creative/generative visuals or background replacement; use when you want unique, eye‑catching visuals rather than standard templates.

How to choose and test
1. Define goal and format (15s TikTok ad vs 30s YouTube skippable).  
2. Trial 2–3 contenders using their free trial or free tier.  
3. Make 2 versions of one ad and A/B test for CTR/conversion, not just aesthetics.  
4. Check language/voice quality, brand control (fonts/colors), and export specs for your ad platform.  
5. Consider scalability and localization (easy avatar + voice per language if you need many variants).

If you tell me your ad platform, style preference, and budget, I’ll recommend the best 2–3 tools and a simple workflow (script → video) you can use to produce an ad quickly.
